abstract: Maintains deep reservoir pressure depletion modeling, 100% reinjection verification plans, and wellfield capital expenditure records
system_message:
You are the Subsurface reservoir engineering lead (RES). Your responsibilities include maintaining deep reservoir pressure depletion modeling, 100% reinjection verification plans, and wellfield capital expenditure records.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Exploratory core sample mineralogy（CORELOG）
information_points.content:
RES-CORELOG-BB6：Core petrology laboratory assays for Reykjanes District Energy Venture show a silica scaling potential index of 1.2 1, representing the calculated saturation index of amorphous silica at 160 degrees Celsius in target production reservoir core samples.
RES-CORELOG-SU8：Core petrology laboratory assays for Nordic GeoPower Alliance show a silica scaling potential index of 1.8 1, representing the calculated saturation index of amorphous silica at 160 degrees Celsius in target production reservoir core samples.
RES-CORELOG-DTA：Core petrology laboratory assays for Borealis Thermal Consortium show a silica scaling potential index of 2.4 1, representing the calculated saturation index of amorphous silica at 160 degrees Celsius in target production reservoir core samples.

information_points.title: Maintains deep reservoir pressure depletion modeling, 100% reinjection verification plans, and wellfield capital expenditure records（GEODEPTH）
information_points.content:
RES-GEODEPTH-6Y4：For Nordic GeoPower Alliance, the deep geothermal reinjection plan is approved based on the National Energy Authority technical validation registry confirming that 100% of extracted geothermal fluid is returned to the production reservoir. Under full winter peak thermal load across 20 years of continuous extraction in the target deep basaltic formation, the modeled annual reservoir pressure depletion rate is 5.4 bar/year, and the guaranteed wellfield drilling capital commitment through 2028 is 48,000,000 EUR.
RES-GEODEPTH-XTC：For Borealis Thermal Consortium, the deep geothermal reinjection plan is approved based on the National Energy Authority technical validation registry confirming that 100% of extracted geothermal fluid is returned to the production reservoir. Under full winter peak thermal load across 20 years of continuous extraction in the target deep basaltic formation, the modeled annual reservoir pressure depletion rate is 2.8 bar/year, and the guaranteed wellfield drilling capital commitment through 2028 is 55,500,000 EUR.
RES-GEODEPTH-67U：For Reykjanes District Energy Venture, the deep geothermal reinjection plan is approved based on the National Energy Authority technical validation registry confirming that 100% of extracted geothermal fluid is returned to the production reservoir. Under full winter peak thermal load across 20 years of continuous extraction in the target deep basaltic formation, the modeled annual reservoir pressure depletion rate is 4.5 bar/year, and the guaranteed wellfield drilling capital commitment through 2028 is 42,500,000 EUR.
